Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: GizmoTickler
Message:
feat(chart): panel the last reap-telemetry metrics and make metric drift bidirectional

v1.10.5 added reap telemetry, but two registered metrics reached the chart
with no dashboard panel — and the existing drift test structurally could not
notice, because it only asserted the FORWARD direction (every charted
scale_csi_* token exists in driver.MetricNames()). A one-directional check is
how they were missed.

Panels:
- Guarded GC (stat, OFF/ON value mappings) on reconcile_delete_enabled.
  Without it "reaper idle because nothing to do" and "reaper idle because
  gated GC is switched off" are indistinguishable on every other panel.
- Unknown-Age Tombstones (stat) on tombstone_unknown_age. These are EXCLUDED
  from tombstone_oldest_age_seconds, so the oldest-age panel structurally
  cannot show them; the description states that caveat.
- volume_quota_bytes added to Per-Volume Usage. The new reverse check found it
  referenced nowhere — invisible to a live-registry survey because these
  volumes are zvols with no quota, so the metric never appears in a scrape.

Drift test, now bidirectional:
- Reverse: every metric in driver.MetricNames() must be referenced by the
  dashboard or a chart PrometheusRule (unobservedMetrics, empty).
- Dashboard-only: every registered metric must be PANELED (unpaneledMetrics,
  empty). Dashboard-OR-rule alone does not deliver "never silently lose a
  panel" — an alert reference satisfies it.

Extraction is now a real PromQL parse (prometheus/promql/parser, walking
VectorSelector) rather than a substring scan, after the substring and
hand-lexer forms were each shown to be satisfiable without querying the
metric. Seven bypass classes are pinned by tests: string literals (double,
single, raw/backtick), embedded-prefix identifiers, hidden targets, grouping
labels in by()/without(), and label matcher names. Exact __name__ matchers
deliberately DO count. Panels nested in collapsed rows are traversed — that
masks nothing today, which is exactly why it is fixed now rather than
discovered when someone collapses a row. Parse errors fail the test loudly
instead of silently yielding zero refs.

The same identifier-boundary fix closes a pre-existing FORWARD hole:
fake_scale_csi_foo no longer tokenizes as scale_csi_foo.

prometheus/prometheus is a test-only dependency; `go list -deps ./cmd/scale-csi`
shows zero references and govulncheck is clean.

Release notes: both invariants described distinctly, and the historical
v1.10.4 "55-metric registry" corrected to 63 (54 helper-registered plus 9
custom backend-health).

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: GizmoTickler
Message:
sprint5-o13: reaper-refusal, provenance-overflow, and CHAP-failure Events (O13,O14,O15)

- O13: emit one aggregated ReaperRefused Warning Event per reconcile pass when
  manual-recovery tombstones are present, and one ReconcileGuardRefusal event for
  non-cap guard refusals. Both target the controller Node ref (cluster-scoped).
- O14: emit a FencingProvenanceOverflow Warning Event on the PV at the
  publish-refusal site (ResourceExhausted) so the publish-blocking condition is
  visible without scraping controller logs.
- O15: add util.ErrISCSICHAPConfig (distinct from ErrISCSIAuthFailure) wrapping
  the already-redacted CHAP param-set failure, and emit an ISCSICHAPFailed Warning
  Event in the NodeStage path. The event message carries only the parameter name
  and exit class — never the username/password (verified by test).

New event reasons: ReaperRefused, ReconcileGuardRefusal,
FencingProvenanceOverflow, ISCSICHAPFailed.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: GizmoTickler
Message:
sprint5-fix: M1 make the metric-drift test render+decode and close false negatives

The old test scanned raw template bytes with scale_csi_[a-z0-9_]+ and blindly
stripped _bucket/_sum/_count, so it missed: a fake _count on a gauge, colon
recording-rule references (truncated at the colon), and it treated
recording-rule output names as driver references.

Rewrite it to render both templates and extract the actual expr fields
(dashboard panel targets; PrometheusRule alert/record rules), so comments,
descriptions, and record outputs are not mistaken for metric refs. Tokenize
with a namespace-anchored regex that retains full colon-bearing names and
uppercase. Permit _bucket/_sum/_count ONLY on histogram/summary bases (new
driver.HistogramMetricNames()), accept chart-defined recording-rule outputs,
and reject unknown colon names. Add a validation table pinning every case from
the review (dashboard/rule typo, fake _count on a gauge, colon refs, recording
output). A full PromQL parser is deliberately avoided (would pull in the
Prometheus server module). Verified the test still fails on a rule typo and on
a fake _count on a gauge.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: GizmoTickler
Message:
sprint2-fix: X8 stateful fence/clone/replay/rotation tests, updated goldens + csi-sanity CHAP

- Real applyISCSIFence over CHAP volumes (strict + additive, publish + unpublish)
  asserts every rebuilt group keeps authmethod+auth=tag; stored-mode drives
  CHAP_MUTUAL regardless of the flipped global flag (X1/X2/X8).
- X1 fatal-stamp: injected CHAP-prop write failure fails CreateVolume and rolls
  back the dataset; retry stamps durably.
- X3 clone scrub + request-wins tests; X4 four-matrix policy guard + stable
  volume-context replay + non-CHAP->CHAP rejection.
- X5 hot-cache collision (cache NOT cleared), rotation calls ISCSIAuthUpdate with
  a stable tag, duplicate-tag reconcile (adopt winner / fail on identity
  mismatch).
- Golden CreateVolume fresh iSCSI CHAP 16->17 (added post-create duplicate-tag
  verification query); breakdown documented. 14/10 unchanged.
- csi-sanity: dedicated controller-only iSCSI CHAP context + secrets file; the
  default non-CHAP iSCSI/NFS suites are unchanged.

Author: GizmoTickler
Message:
docs(reference): map the live TrueNAS 26.0 API and gap-analyze driver usage

Captured core.get_methods from the production TrueNAS 26.0.0-BETA.2
instance (805 methods) so development targets true API capabilities
instead of assumptions: raw JSON dump, per-service method map, and a
knob-by-knob gap analysis of the 88 methods the driver calls plus 167
relevant uncalled methods with roles, job flags, and ranked value.

Description: Detected a Generic API Key, potentially exposing access to various services and sensitive operations.
Author: GizmoTickler
Message:
fix(security): get the CHAP password off argv, redact secret-bearing backend errors

1. HIGH — the iSCSI CHAP password was passed as 'iscsiadm -v <secret>', and the
   node DaemonSet runs hostPID, so the plaintext sat in THREE simultaneous
   argvs (bash wrapper, nsenter, host iscsiadm) with /proc/<pid>/cmdline
   world-readable. Reading it needed neither root nor privileged: any pod with
   hostPID in a namespace admitted as privileged could poll /proc. The credential
   is shared per StorageClass, so it authorizes login for every volume on it.

   authmethod/username/username_in stay on argv; both password fields are now
   written directly into the open-iscsi node record at 0600, atomically via a
   temp file staged in the DB root (never the record dir, where idbm would read
   a stray file as another iface record), secrets last so no later -o update can
   follow the chmod.

   Feeding 'iscsiadm -o update' from a file does NOT work — upstream has no
   file-borne value input, -v is the only way to pass a value, so that variant
   would still end with the secret in argv. Writing the record is the only
   approach that removes it from all three.

   Fail-closed: if no node record exists, staging errors rather than falling back
   to argv, because a silent fallback would restore the vulnerability while
   looking fixed.

2. MEDIUM — pool.dataset.create takes the passphrase as a call argument and its
   raw error reached the tenant's own PVC Event plus a V(0) log. The driver
   already redacts unlock and change_key for exactly this reason; create was
   missed. Wrapped so Error() is masked while Unwrap() stays intact, so
   errors.Is/As classification upstack is unchanged.

3. MEDIUM — iscsi.auth.create/update had no redaction at all; redactCHAP only
   ever handled maps. Added redactCHAPError and used it at both call sites.

Also removed cmd/debug-api's -api-key flag, which its own --help recommended;
TRUENAS_API_KEY already worked.

docs/production.md carried an explicit 'accepted exposure' bullet stating the
credential is visible in /proc. Leaving it would have told operators the fix had
not happened; rewritten to describe the argv exposure as closed and keep the
genuine residual, that node root can read the clear-text node DB.

Co-authored-by: scale-csi security fixer <noreply@localhost>
